label: early original-phase input of m/k/j/h/digits after b/m/p/q-like prefix
explanation: Fires almost only in the original (input) phase at early positions t=1..5. Most of the mass is at t=2-3, and it is never active at t=0, at the delimiter, or in the copy phase (25 stray steps). Two things drive it, and they look additive: the current input token (m, k, 3, j, h, 1 strongest, then o, 2, e, t, g) and which tokens came earlier in the prefix (b strongest, then m, p, q, 3, u). The largest activations come from b-initial prefixes followed by k or m, e.g. b b [k] or b b [m]. It favours the first occurrence of a token (in_first carries 91% of the mass). Seen-prefix AND current-token conjunction: dev F1 0.62, mass recall 0.82. Position alone gets about 98% mass recall but only 0.16 precision. The behaviour looks graded, a token-weighted sum, so a boolean rule cannot fully capture it.
